items.stem: Whom does Creon address at the start of his first speech?
options: The elders
The army of Argos
His son and his wife
The priests of Zeus

items.stem: By what right does Creon claim the throne?
options: Kinship to the princes
Victory in single combat
Election by the people
A command from Delphi

items.stem: To what does Creon compare the State?
options: A ship carrying all
A house built on rock
A tree with many branches
A flock that needs a shepherd

items.stem: Complete Creon's line: “I’ve posted guards to watch the _____.”
options: palace
corpse
treasury
altar

items.stem: What news does the Guard bring?
options: Dust was sprinkled on the body
The Argive army has returned
A riot has broken out in the city
The guards have run away

items.stem: Why does the Guard come so slowly?
options: He fears the king's anger
He was wounded in the battle
He stopped to pray at a temple
He lost his way in the dark

items.stem: Whom does Creon suspect of being behind the burial?
options: Men with bribes
The gods themselves
The priests of the city
Soldiers from Argos

items.stem: Complete Creon's claim: “Money ’tis that sacks _____, and drives men forth from hearth and home”
options: Temples
Harvests
Cities
Rivers

items.stem: Why does Creon say he chose the elders as councillors?
options: They were loyal to the royal line
They fought bravely in the war
They are the richest men in Thebes
They are related to him by blood

items.stem: Complete Creon's line: “Farewell to friendship, if she suffers _____.”
options: wreck
honour
triumph
praise

items.stem: What did the guards find around the body?
options: No sign of digging or wheels
Footprints leading to the palace
A torn piece of a woman's robe
A broken spear by the grave

items.stem: How was the Guard chosen to bring the news?
options: The guards cast lots
He volunteered
Creon summoned him by name
The others forced him at sword point

items.stem: What does Creon mean when he says that a ruler “tongue-tied By fear” is the basest of the base?
options: A ruler must speak out for the State
A ruler must not take advice from anyone
A ruler must hide his fears from the people
A ruler must speak only through heralds

items.stem: How does the Chorus first react to the Guard's news?
options: It wonders if the gods did it
It demands that the guards be punished
It praises the person who buried him
It says nothing at all

items.stem: Why does Creon reject the Chorus's suggestion?
options: He thinks the gods would not honour a traitor
He believes the gods do not exist
He thinks the Chorus is plotting with the guards
He fears that the Chorus is right

items.stem: What is ironic about Creon's speech on the duty of rulers to accept good counsel?
options: He rejects the first counsel he hears
He asks the guards for their advice
He resigns from the throne at once
He agrees with every word the Chorus says

items.stem: What does Creon mean by “Till he be proved by exercise of power”?
options: Power reveals a man's character
A man must win a war before he can rule
Power should go only to the old
A king must prove his birth before he rules

items.stem: Complete the Chorus's line: “No man is mad enough to court his _____.”
options: honour
office
fortune
death

items.stem: Why does the Guard say “I will speak though I say nothing”?
options: He has news but no culprit
He has been told to keep the matter secret
He has forgotten the message he carried
He plans to lie to the king

items.stem: What does the Guard's account of the burial suggest about the deed?
options: It was secret and left no trace
It was done by a large band of men
It was done in daylight before the guards
It was done by wild animals

items.stem: What is the tone of Creon's words “I am like to think you dote in your old age”?
options: Contemptuous
Grateful
Sorrowful
Amused

items.stem: Which device is at work in the Guard's line about a furlong becoming a league?
options: Hyperbole
Simile
Personification
Alliteration

items.stem: What does the episode suggest about Creon as a new ruler?
options: He fears disorder and treats dissent as treason
He is gentle and slow to anger
He trusts the gods above his own judgment
He wants to divide power with the elders

items.stem: What does Creon mean by “the guerdon of the heroic dead”?
options: The honours owed to those who die for the city
The treasure buried with a king
The fame that poets give to heroes
The punishment for traitors

items.stem: Complete the Guard's line: “The bearer of dread tidings needs must _____.”
options: rejoice
boast
quake
rest

items.stem: What effect does the Guard's phrase “thirsty dust” create?
options: It makes the earth seem to welcome the rite
It shows that the land is in a drought
It suggests the guards were careless
It hints that the body has been moved

items.stem: Why does the Guard mention the ordeal of red-hot iron?
options: To prove how desperately the guards swore their innocence
To describe the torture Creon has ordered
To explain how the body was burned
To show the guards' skill as smiths

items.stem: What is the dramatic effect of Creon's long speech before the Guard enters?
options: It sets out the principle that the news will test
It shows that Creon has no plans at all
It reveals who performed the burial
It ends the conflict before it begins

items.stem: How does the scene complicate the audience's view of Creon?
options: His principles sound reasonable but his anger is rash
He seems wise in every way
He shows no interest in the city
He openly admits that his edict is wrong
